the radiative decays of the upsilon family are very weak, and that off-shell suppressions are very large.

the radiative decay rates of UPSILON and its first radial excitation UPSILON' are generally too small to be directly observed, and that the off-shell coupling constants of the two states are suppressed by about a factor of 1/100 compared with their onshell values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the radiative decay of upsilon (upsilon') into lepton-antilepton pair and photon.
a detailed study of the properties of the radiative processes of the UPSILON and UPSION' resonances.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiative decays of UPSILON and of UPSILON' are very difficult to detect and the radiative decaying modes of UPSILON' and of UPSILON are even less accessible.
the radiative processes of the UPSILON and UPSILLON' mesons are very unlikely to be observed directly.
the radiative decays of UPSILON and its first excited state are not likely to be observed in the foreseeable future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the radiative decays of UPSILON and its prime are not expected to be very important experimentally, and that the off-shell suppressions of the coupling constants should be taken into account when one considers the radiative processes involving off-shell UPSILON.
the radiative decays of UPSILON and its first radial excitation are too weak to be observed directly in the near future.

, in the present scheme, the radiative processes of psi and UPSILON are well understood, and the radiative processes involving UPSILON' can only be understood if one assumes that the off-shell coupling constants of UPSILON' are strongly suppressed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiative decays of UPSILON and the off-shell UPSILON coupling constants are not very important for the phenomenology of these states.
the radiative decays of UPSILON and its first radial excitation are too small for direct experimental observation.
the off-shell suppressions of the radiative decay widths of UPSILON and the off-shell coupling constants are not negligible.
